sources.title: Picqer - Warehouse software for online stores and fulfilment
Picqer Pricing - Easy plans for every size
Hardware and robots in your warehouse
Changelog: easier communication and more (29 Oct 2026)
Katapull breidt Commerce Hub uit met overname van Picqer (7 Oct 2026)
Katapull buys WMS provider Picqer to fill out its Commerce Hub
Integratie met Picqer voor magazijn en voorraadbeheer

items.title: Picqer targets 25 to 5,000+ orders a day with self-service setup
items.summary: Picqer says it helps from about 25 orders a day, that the ideal size is 25 to 5,000 orders a day, that it can be set up in one day (warehouses usually need one to two weeks of preparation) and that most customers set it up themselves; it also states it is "for online stores and fulfilment companies that operate their own warehouse" shipping products as received (no assemblies).
items.implication: The model treats self-service onboarding and time to first shipped order as core; assembly/kitting and manufacturing are out of scope.

items.title: Order-volume pricing with unlimited users and stores
items.summary: Published online-store plans run from Team (EUR 379/month, 3,000 orders included, EUR 0.28 per extra order) through Business (EUR 825), Premium (EUR 1,349), Premium+ (EUR 2,475) to Enterprise (EUR 5,500/month, 75,000 orders, EUR 0.055 per extra order). All features, unlimited users and stores and unlimited support are included; payment by card or SEPA direct debit; 14-day trial.
items.implication: Revenue grows with customers' order volume, so customer growth and retention drive Picqer growth; feature gating is not a lever.

items.title: Picqer Fulfilment serves more than 80 fulfilment companies
items.summary: Picqer reports more than 80 fulfilment companies and thousands of webshops using Picqer daily. Fulfilment plans start at EUR 825/month (3,000 orders, EUR 0.25 extra) with Plus (EUR 2,475), Next (EUR 3,850) and Max (on request, 90,000 orders); there are no setup or per-client fees.
items.implication: Fulfilment is a distinct segment with its own pricing, portal and invoicing needs; per-client fee absence is a competitive argument.

items.title: Market-leader claim in the Netherlands
items.summary: Picqer states that "10% of all online orders in the Netherlands are processed with Picqer" and calls itself the market leader in the Netherlands. These are self-reported claims without a published method.
items.implication: Use as positioning, not as a market-share statistic; Dutch home-market saturation makes Belgium, Germany and Commerce Hub cross-selling relevant growth levers (inference).

items.title: Founded 2012, profitable and without external investors before Katapull
items.summary: Picqer started in November 2012 after its founders built custom web applications for seven years; it describes itself as profitable with no external investors and working with few meetings and asynchronous communication. Co-founders named on the team page are Casper and Stephan; Casper Bakker is quoted as co-founder in the acquisition release.
items.implication: A product-led, low-overhead culture is part of the value proposition ("software without a manual"); integration into Katapull should not dilute it.

items.title: Katapull acquired Picqer on 7 October 2026 to complete its Commerce Hub
items.summary: Katapull announced the acquisition of Picqer (deal value undisclosed; described as a "miljoenendeal") on 7 October 2026, adding warehouse management, order processing and inventory to its Commerce Hub. Both target mid-market commerce. Katapull positions Picqer as the next step for Logic4 customers whose warehouse needs exceed Logic4's functionality. Picqer's co-founder mentioned even better integration with long-standing partners Returnista and DeliveryMatch.
items.implication: Hub bridges (Logic4, DeliveryMatch, Returnista) and co-selling become strategic; Picqer must stay an open platform for non-Katapull partners.

items.title: Integrations with siblings are partly evidenced already
items.summary: Picqer lists DeliveryMatch ("Integration by DeliveryMatch") and Returnista on its integrations page; DeliveryMatch publishes a Picqer integration page; Picqer's blog describes Returnista pre-registering returns in Picqer; Transus and Vendit publish Picqer partner pages within the Katapull partner set. No Logic4, Highbiza or EffectConnect integration with Picqer was found.
items.implication: Model DeliveryMatch and Returnista bridges as facts; Logic4, Transus, Vendit, Highbiza and EffectConnect flows as assumptions.

items.title: Walking and singles dominate picking effort
items.summary: Picqer states that order pickers generally walk 60-80% of their workday and that for an average online store 60-70% of orders are single-line "singles", which its singles picking handles about twice as fast. Batch picking can combine e.g. 12 orders in one route. These are vendor statements without a cited study.
items.implication: Route optimisation, batching and singles are the main productivity levers for webshop warehouses.

items.title: Customer quotes centre on labour savings and easy onboarding
items.summary: Cases quote "one employee can do the work of 4 or 5 people" (Alleeninkt.nl), "without Picqer we would need at least 6 or 7 extra staffers" (Boozyshop), getting "a student up and running in 5 minutes" (Bernard Roerdink), and Alleeninkt.nl reports 1 million orders processed through Picqer by 2025.
items.implication: Testimonials, not measured benchmarks; they support the persona focus on labour productivity and new-staff onboarding.

items.title: Batch traceability shipped; client invoicing in development
items.summary: Picqer Fulfilment announces batch number and best-before tracking through stock, moves, picks, counts and returns, visible in the fulfilment portal, as new; client invoicing that links rates to picklists, shipments, receipts, returns and storage is "in development".
items.implication: Year-1 fulfilment roadmap in the model follows Picqer's own announcements; invoicing adoption targets are assumptions.

items.title: Hardware path from packing table to AutoStore
items.summary: Picqer describes three hardware steps: packing-table hardware (label printers, slip printers, scanners), mobile handhelds (Zebra, Honeywell; the Zebra TC22 is named as favourite), then mechanisation and robots (carton sealers, label applicators, conveyors, goods-to-person systems such as Kardex and AutoStore, picking robots) with Dutch intralogistics partners.
items.implication: Hardware support lets Picqer retain accounts as they scale, competing with enterprise WMS at the top of its range.

items.title: Dutch WMS competition includes 3PL-owned software and webshop WMS
items.summary: Monta offers MontaWMS (25+ years in its own fulfilment warehouses, 20+ warehouses in Europe) alongside fulfilment and MontaShip; GoedGepickt says orders of more than 4,500 webshops are processed daily with its WMS and it connects with 70+ platforms.
items.implication: Picqer competes both with SaaS WMS for webshops and with 3PLs that bundle their own WMS; ease of use and openness must stay ahead.

items.title: Collaboration features target peak and fulfilment clients
items.summary: The 29 October 2026 changelog adds reactions and up to five photos on comments, a "For you" inbox, e-mail notifications, client mentions in the portal, copying users and a rights overview, picklist splitting, GS1 barcodes with lot/expiry, DataMatrix and QR scanning in the app, and concept orders for fulfilment clients.
items.implication: Collaboration and client self-service are active investment areas; modelled as an invest brick.
